description: Step-based explanation tool for Grade 7 Mathematics — Token Model for Integer Subtraction. Walks students through the token model using a concrete worked example (default: 7 − 18). Each step progressively reveals a key phase: starting tokens, adding zero pairs, removing tokens, counting what remains, and generalising to the additive inverse rule. Indian school context (NCERT Ganita Prakash Grade 7).
subject: Mathematics
topic: Operations with Integers — Token Model Recap: Addition, Subtraction, and Additive Inverse

minuend.description: The number being subtracted from (a in a − b). Should be a positive integer for the visual model to work correctly.

subtrahend.description: The number being subtracted (b in a − b). Should be greater than minuend so that zero pairs are needed, demonstrating the concept.

showTeachingNotes.description: If true, show teaching notes alongside student instructions (for teacher mode)

constraints: minuend should be a non-negative integer
subtrahend should be greater than minuend for the tool to meaningfully demonstrate zero pairs
Both values should be small enough for visual clarity (recommended: minuend ≤ 15, subtrahend ≤ 25)

learn.label: Learn
learn.description: Step-through explanation mode — the primary and default mode for this tool.

details.title: Place the Starting Tokens
details.visual: Green (+1) tokens appear one by one with pop-in animation
details.teachingNote: Ask students to count tokens and notice the shortfall when they need to remove more than they have.

details.title: Add Zero Pairs
details.visual: Green-red pairs slide in from side, labelled 'zero pair' with bracket showing = 0
details.teachingNote: Ask what a zero pair is and why adding one doesn't change the total.

details.title: Remove Green Tokens
details.visual: Green tokens fade out with ✕ mark, only red tokens remain
details.teachingNote: Demonstrate the removal visually. Ask students to predict what remains.

details.title: Count What Remains
details.visual: Remaining red tokens pulse once and a result badge animates in showing the answer
details.teachingNote: Ask students to state the answer before revealing the result badge.

details.title: The Additive Inverse Rule
details.visual: Rule card animates into view: 'Subtract b = Add −b (additive inverse)' with concrete example
details.teachingNote: Connect to algebraic rule, then test with: 'If we subtract −12 from 4, what does that become?'

tokens.positive: Bright green circular token with + symbol, radial gradient, inner glow
tokens.negative: Bright red circular token with − symbol, radial gradient, inner glow

design.workspace: Grid-patterned activity mat bordered by thin blue line, resembling a classroom activity mat

teachingNotes.step1: At Step 1, ask: 'How many tokens do we have, and how many do we need to remove?' — let students notice the shortfall.
teachingNotes.step2: At Step 2, ask: 'What is a zero pair and why does adding one not change the total?' — pause for discussion.
teachingNotes.step3: At Step 3, demonstrate the removal visually.
teachingNotes.step4: At Step 4, ask students to read the result before revealing it.
teachingNotes.step5: At Step 5, connect to the algebraic rule: 7 − 18 = 7 + (−18). Then ask: 'If we subtract −12 from 4, what does that become?' to test inverse understanding.

instructionsForStudent.overview: Watch the token workspace change at each step.
instructionsForStudent.step2: Predict: why do we add zero pairs instead of just removing tokens?
instructionsForStudent.step4: Count what remains and form the answer.
instructionsForStudent.step5: State the general rule in your own words before reading it.
